title: The low-speed limit: the mass the body loses
spoken: The limit, as v approaches zero, of 2 L times gamma minus one, over v squared, equals L over c squared.
explanation: At any finite speed the quotient is a little larger than L/c². As the speed shrinks it settles on L/c², the coefficient Newtonian mechanics reads as the mass the body lost. The limit is taken, not set at v = 0, where the quotient is not defined.
assumptions: Two equal, opposite light pulses remove total positive energy L; their symmetry removes recoil in the body’s rest frame.
The same unchanged additive energy offset before and after emission, so the kinetic-energy drop is exactly L(γ − 1).
These are authored modern teaching equations, not a transcription or printed-notation concordance.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: The quotient settles on L/c² as the speed shrinks, whatever the size of L.

notes.title: The limit as v shrinks
notes.explanation: The value the quotient settles on as v gets closer and closer to zero. It is not the quotient at v = 0, which divides by zero.

notes.title: Twice the drop over v²
notes.explanation: The finite-speed quotient. At every finite speed it is a little larger than L/c².

notes.title: Twice the kinetic-energy drop
notes.explanation: 2L(γ − 1): twice the exact drop, so that it compares with the Newtonian ½ m v².

notes.title: The factor's excess over one
notes.explanation: γ − 1, zero at rest. For small speeds it begins with v²/(2c²).

notes.title: Speed squared
notes.explanation: Divide by v² to leave a mass.

notes.title: The coefficient
notes.explanation: L/c²: the energy given off, divided by the square of the speed of light.

notes.title: Observer speed
notes.explanation: The speed of the second observer relative to the body, which the limit shrinks toward zero.

notes.title: Emitted energy L
notes.explanation: Total energy of both opposite pulses, in the body’s rest frame.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: γ for the observer speed v: one at rest, larger at any other speed.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: c, the speed of light in empty space.

sentence.text: shrinks, twice the kinetic-energy drop over its square settles on
